source_text: μάλιστα τῶν ἄλλων ἐξειλεγμέναι καὶ ἱερομύστιδες, τῆς τοιαύτης μόλις ἠξιοῦντο τιμῆς, ὕβρεως μὲν οὖν· ὧδε γὰρ ἄμεινόν τε καὶ ἀληθὲς εἰπεῖν. Γύναια δὴ οὖν τῶν ἐξ αἵματος Ἰσραὴλ, λείψανα τῆς ἐν Αἰγύπτῳ λατρείας ἐν ἰδίοις σκεύεσιν εὑρηκότα, ταυτὶ δὴ τὰ κάτοπτρα προσεκόμισαν εἰς καρποφορίαν, ἃ καὶ εἰς τὸ τοῦ λουτῆρος μετεσκευάσθη χρῆμα. Σκηνῆς δὲ τῆς ἁγίας ἐγηγερμένης νενηστεύκασι προσιζήσαντά που ταῖς θύραις, καὶ πάντα ἁγνῶς διαιτώμενα, ὑποδηλοῦντος, οἶμαι, τοῦ πράγματος, ὅτι τῆς ἀληθεστέρας ἀναδεδειγμένης σκηνῆς, τοῦτ' ἔστι, τῆς Ἐκκλησίας ἣν ἔπηξεν ὁ Κύριος, καὶ οὐκ ἄνθρωπος, ὡς ὁ θεσπέσιος γράφει Παῦλος, καιρὸς ἤδη πως τοὺς ἀνακειμένους εἰς δόξαν ποτὲ τῆς τῶν δαιμονίων ἀγέλης, εἰς ἱερὰ μεταπλάττεσθαι σκεύη, καὶ ἐπιτηδείως ἔχοντα πρὸς παραδοχὴν τοῦ ἁγίου βαπτίσματος, ὡς καὶ διαπρέπειν δύνασθαι τοῖς ὑπὲρ νόμον αὐχήμασιν. Τουτὶ γὰρ, οἶμαι, ἔστι τὸ ἐκ κατόπτρων Ἑλληνικῶν, ἤτοι κειμηλίων διαβολικῶν, τὸν λουτῆρα πλάττεσθαι τὸν χαλκοῦν, ἐν ᾧ δὴ καὶ τὸ ὕδωρ, τὸ καὶ αὐτὸν ἀποκαθαῖρον Μωσέα, καὶ τῇ κατὰ νόμον ἱερωσύνῃ χρήσιμον εἰς ἀπόνιψιν, δῆλον δὲ ὅτι τὴν νοητήν. Ἢ γὰρ, οὐχὶ σκεύη διαβολικὰ, τοὺς πεπλανημένους καὶ τοῖς δαιμονίοις λελατρευκότας φαίης ἂν εἶναι καὶ αὐτὸς, ὦ Παλλάδιε; {ΠΑΛΛ.} Πῶς γὰρ οὔ; {ΚΥΡ.} Νενηστεύκασι δὲ τὰ γύναια παρὰ τὰς θύρας τῆς σκηνῆς τῆς ἁγίας. Εἴη δ' ἂν καὶ τάδε καλὸν αἴνιγμα καὶ σοφὸν, τοῦ μὴ δι' αἱμάτων εἰστρέχειν ἐν ἐκκλησίαις τοὺς ἐν Χριστῷ δεδικαιωμένους, θυσίαις δὲ μᾶλλον πνευματικαῖς ἐκπρέποντας, καὶ δωροφορίαν ὥσπερ τινὰ προσκομίζοντας τῷ Θεῷ τὴν ἐγκράτειαν, τὴν οἱονεὶ νέκρωσιν τῆς σαρκός. «Παραστήσατε γὰρ,» φησὶ, «τὰ σώματα ὑμῶν, θυσίαν ζῶσαν, ἁγίαν, εὐάρεστον τῷ Θεῷ, τὴν λογικὴν λατρείαν ὑμῶν.» Καὶ πάλιν· «Δοξάσατε δὴ τὸν Θεὸν ἐν τῷ σώματι ὑμῶν.» Οὐκοῦν αἱ νηστεύσασαι τῆς ἁγίας ἐγηγερμένης σκηνῆς, εἰς εἰκόνα τελοῦσι ψυχῶν, οὐ Μωσαϊκοῖς ἐντάλμασι παιδαγωγουμένων ἔτι, πνευματικὴν δὲ μᾶλλον καὶ εὐαγγελικὴν ἀναδεδειγμένων τὴν πολιτείαν ἤδη, καὶ πατουσῶν οὐκ ἀνιδρωτὶ τὰς ἐπιγείους ἡδονὰς, καὶ ἀναμορφουμένων εὖ μάλα πρὸς τὸ ἀκήρατον κάλλος, διὰ τὸ μὴ ἀνέχεσθαι παθεῖν τὰ μυσαρά τε καὶ βέβηλα τῆς φιλοσαρκίας ἐγκλήματα. Ἢ οὐχ οὕτως ἡμῖν ὁ τοῦ βίου τρόπος τοῖς ἐν Χριστῷ κεκλημένοις εἰς ἁγιασμὸν καὶ ἰσχνότητα τὴν πνευματικήν; {ΠΑΛΛ.} Πάνυ μὲν οὖν. {ΚΥΡ.} Ἀλλὰ ταυτὶ μὲν εἰς τὸ παρὸν σκευῶν ἱερῶν εἰρήσθω πέρι. Φέρε δὲ, εἰ δοκεῖ, καὶ αὐτὴν ἡμῖν ὅπως ἔχει θέσεώς τε καὶ κατασκευῆς κατασκεπτώμεθα τὴν σκηνήν. Καὶ βαθὺ μὲν τὸ χρῆμα, καὶ τῶν καθ' ἡμᾶς ἐπέκεινα μέτρων, βλάβος δὲ οἶμαι τὸ σύμπαν οὐδὲν, πανταχόθεν ἡμᾶς ἐρανίζεσθαι φιλεῖν τὸ τελοῦν εἰς ὄνησιν, καὶ τοῖς ἄγαν ὑπερκειμένοις ὡς ἔνι προσβάλλοντας.
pass_a_gloss: [cont. from s.22: Egyptian women entering temples with mirror in left hand and sistrum in right] who as most of all (ὅτι μάλιστα) chosen out (ἐξειλεγμέναι) from the others and temple-initiates (ἱερομύστιδες) were scarcely deemed worthy (μόλις ἠξιοῦντο) of such honour (τιμή) — of outrage (ὕβρις) rather; for so it is better and true to say. Women (γύναια) then of those from Israel’s blood, having found (εὑρηκότα) remnants (λείψανα) of the worship (λατρεία) in Egypt in their own vessels/belongings (σκεύη), brought (προσεκόμισαν) these mirrors (κάτοπτρα) for an offering (καρποφορία), which were also refashioned (μετεσκευάσθη) into the matter of the laver (λουτήρ). The holy tent (σκηνή) having been raised (ἐγηγερμένης), they fasted (νενηστεύκασι), sitting by (προσιζήσαντα) somewhere at the doors (θύραι) and living (διαιτώμενα) all things purely (ἁγνῶς); the event hinting (ὑποδηλοῦντος), I think, that the truer tent having been shown (ἀναδεδειγμένης), that is, the Church (Ἐκκλησία) which the Lord pitched (ἔπηξεν) and not man, as the inspired (θεσπέσιος) Paul writes, it is now somehow time (καιρός) for those once dedicated (ἀνακειμένους) to the glory (δόξα) of the herd (ἀγέλη) of demons (δαιμόνια) to be reshaped (μεταπλάττεσθαι) into holy vessels (ἱερὰ σκεύη), and being fit (ἐπιτηδείως ἔχοντα) for reception (παραδοχή) of holy baptism (βάπτισμα), so as to be able to excel (διαπρέπειν) with boasts beyond law (ὑπὲρ νόμον αὐχήμασιν). For this, I think, is the forming of the bronze laver from Hellenic (= pagan) mirrors, that is, devilish treasures (κειμήλια διαβολικά), in which is the water that cleansed (ἀποκαθαῖρον) even Moses himself and useful to the priesthood (ἱερωσύνη) according to law for washing (ἀπόνιψις) — clearly the intelligible/spiritual (νοητήν) one. Or would you not say yourself, Palladius, that the deceived (πεπλανημένους) and those who served demons are devilish vessels? PALL.: For how not? CYR.: The women fasted by the doors of the holy tent. This too would be a fine and wise riddle (αἴνιγμα): that those justified (δεδικαιωμένους) in Christ do not run into churches through bloods (αἵματα), but rather are conspicuous (ἐκπρέποντας) by spiritual sacrifices (θυσίαι πνευματικαί), and bring to God as a gift-offering (δωροφορία) self-control (ἐγκράτεια), as it were the deadening (νέκρωσις) of the flesh (σάρξ). [Rom 12:1] ‘Present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, well-pleasing to God, your rational worship (λογικὴ λατρεία).’ And again [1 Cor 6:20] ‘Glorify God in your body.’ So those who fasted when the holy tent was raised fulfil the image (εἰκών) of souls no longer tutored (παιδαγωγουμένων) by Mosaic injunctions (ἐντάλματα), but having already shown a spiritual and evangelical way of life (πολιτεία), and treading (πατουσῶν) not without sweat (ἀνιδρωτί) the earthly pleasures (ἡδοναί), and being re-formed (ἀναμορφουμένων) very well toward unsullied beauty (ἀκήρατον κάλλος), through not enduring to suffer the loathsome and profane charges/offences (ἐγκλήματα) of flesh-love (φιλοσαρκία). Or is not so the manner of life for us called in Christ to sanctification (ἁγιασμός) and spiritual leanness (ἰσχνότης)? PALL.: Entirely so. CYR.: Let these things be said for the present about holy vessels. Come, if it seems good, let us also examine the tent itself, how it holds as to placement (θέσις) and construction (κατασκευή). Deep is the matter and beyond our measures; but I think no harm at all that we love to collect (ἐρανίζεσθαι) from everywhere what leads to profit (ὄνησις), attacking (προσβάλλοντας) as far as possible the things lying very far above.
pass_b_english: Cyril: …chosen out above all the others and initiated into the rites, were barely counted worthy of such an honor, or rather of such an outrage, for that is the better and truer word. So some women of Israel’s blood found among their own belongings these remnants of the worship in Egypt, and they brought these very mirrors as an offering, and the mirrors were made over into the laver (Exodus 38:8). When the holy tent had been set up, they fasted, sitting somewhere by its doors and living purely in everything (Exodus 38:8). The event hints, I think, at this: once the truer tent had been revealed, that is, the Church, which the Lord pitched, and not man, as the inspired Paul writes (Hebrews 8:2), it is now, in a way, time for those once devoted to the glory of the herd of demons to be remade into holy vessels, fit to receive holy baptism, so that they too could shine with glories beyond the law. For this, I think, is what it means that the bronze laver was fashioned out of pagan mirrors, that is, out of the devil’s treasures. In it is the water that cleansed even Moses himself (Exodus 40:31) and served the priesthood under the law for washing (Exodus 30:19–21), a washing plainly to be understood spiritually. Or would you not say yourself, Palladius, that those who have gone astray and worshipped demons are vessels of the devil?

Cyril: The women fasted beside the doors of the holy tent. This too would be a fine and wise riddle. It shows that those who have been justified in Christ do not hurry into the churches by means of blood, but are distinguished rather by spiritual sacrifices, and bring to God, as a kind of gift, their self-control, which is, so to speak, a putting to death of the flesh. For he says: ‘Present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable to God, which is your reasonable worship’ (Romans 12:1). And again: ‘Glorify God in your body’ (1 Corinthians 6:20). So the women who fasted when the holy tent had been set up stand as an image of souls that are no longer schooled by the commandments of Moses, but have already shown forth a spiritual and gospel way of life. Such souls tread down earthly pleasures, not without sweat, and are being thoroughly reshaped toward a beauty without stain, because they will not bear to fall into the foul and profane offences of love of the flesh. Or is this not the manner of life for us who have been called in Christ to sanctification and spiritual leanness?

Cyril: Let this be enough for now about the holy vessels. Come, if you agree, let us also look closely at the tent itself, how it was placed and how it was built. The matter is deep and beyond our measure. Yet I think there is no harm at all in our being eager to gather from every side what makes for our profit, and in reaching, as far as we can, toward things that lie far above us.

choices.why: ‘ἰσχνότης’ (leanness, i.e. the thinness of fasting) kept as ‘spiritual leanness’.

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Cyril De adoratione Book 9 exists. Translated fresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the earlier English of this book was not used as a base.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Section opens mid-sentence, continuing Cyril’s account (end of s.22) of Egyptian priestesses carrying a mirror and a sistrum; ‘ὅτι μάλιστα’ is split across the break and taken with ‘chosen out above all the others’. The mirrors of the women who fasted at the doors of the tent: LXX Exodus 38:26 = English Exodus 38:8; the LXX reads ‘fasted’ (νηστευσασῶν) where the Hebrew has ‘served/ministered’, which is why Cyril speaks of fasting. ‘Ἑλληνικῶν’ rendered ‘pagan’ (Cyril’s usual sense). The water that ‘cleansed even Moses’ refers to Exodus 40:31 (Moses, Aaron and his sons washed at the laver); Exodus 30:19–21 for the priests’ washing. ‘θυσίαις πνευματικαῖς’ echoes 1 Peter 2:5 and ‘κεκλημένοις εἰς ἁγιασμόν’ echoes 1 Thessalonians 4:7; both left uncited as general phrasing. ‘νέκρωσις τῆς σαρκός’ may echo Colossians 3:5 / 2 Corinthians 4:10; uncited. ‘ἰσχνότης’ (leanness, i.e. the thinness of fasting) kept as ‘spiritual leanness’.

changes: καιρὸς ἤδη: 'the time had come' -> 'it is now, in a way, time' (present, as in the Greek)
ἐν ᾧ δὴ καὶ τὸ ὕδωρ: 'was' -> 'is' (no past verb in the Greek)
ἀναμορφουμένων εὖ μάλα πρὸς τὸ ἀκήρατον κάλλος: stiff 'refashioned very well toward a pure beauty' -> 'thoroughly reshaped toward a beauty without stain'
Checked Exodus 38:8 (LXX 38:26), Hebrews 8:2, Exodus 40:31, Exodus 30:19–21, Romans 12:1, 1 Corinthians 6:20: all correct
